method: Faithful vector reconstruction from published raster artwork. Figure 3 labels derive from live overlay source keys in body.tex mapped through references.tex bibliography order; checked against page 8 of main.pdf. SVG lettering outlined from the embedded-font PDFs.

figures.title: Four domains of AI safety activity
figures.alt: A: improve and qualify behavior. B: observe and manage live behavior. C: design bounded execution. D: verify and enforce each action. Cryptographic verifiability connects all four domains.

figures.title: Assurance types for linked claims
figures.alt: Shared RDF and JSON-LD semantics link Q qualified authority, E issuer-authenticated verifiable evidence and U self-asserted information. Each claim requires its own issuer, proof and status checks.

figures.title: Qualitative placement of ten company cases
figures.alt: Filled circles mark primary and open circles supporting activities across A to D. Spherity D and C are research and integration design. Citation labels match the edition 2.6 published overlays.

figures.title: AI Safety Atlas: twenty selected organizations in eight countries
figures.alt: Map and alphabetical lists of ten commercial companies and ten research organizations in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Germany, China, Japan, Singapore and Australia. Teal circles represent companies; ochre diamonds represent research organizations. Filled A–D badges show primary activity and outlined badges supporting activity.

figures.title: Spherity’s proposed runtime assurance architecture
figures.alt: Policy, domain and episode graphs feed admission and coordinated containment. An independent local stop works during model, graph, network and identity-service outages. Stops override admission at the resource boundary. Safe resumption requires verified recovery and separate authorization.
